Rule coefficients are GRN-gated and evolved, so learning windows emerge. Local, bio-inspired, evolutionary, and keeps the clockless kernel. The runtime is the exact kernel, so the sim-to-hardware gap is zero, and Loihi and ReckOn show trace-based learning in silicon. weff[DMAX][2] already exists, so the change is small. Its 'timing teaches direction' test is the cheapest decisive visible result on offer (under 1 CPU-h on s5 with the chemistry knocked out). Weaknesses: search stays a slow GA on CPU, wiring is nearest-neighbour only, and plasticity pays only if worlds vary within a life.

scores.name: A. Maturing tissue: GPU neural-CA cells with neutral division and evolved plasticity
scores.why: Best single design for the user's core sentence. Per-edge three-factor plasticity learned within the life, daughters inheriting the learned face table, and silent newborns that fade in make division function-preserving, which attacks the 0.19 F per-child loss. It keeps the GRN (interpretability, continuity) and one life. ES with 64-256 common-random-number (CRN) lives per genome attacks the Poisson noise. The runtime is a small per-tile datapath plus per-face weight and trace registers. Weaknesses: too many parts at once (GRU plus GRN plus plasticity plus maturation gain, which is redundant), the maturation gain is a new fixed rule, and lockstep training needs the async/clockless gate.

scores.name: Shared in-context cell on GPU: one meta-learned recurrent rule in every cell, vector messages, evolution strategies over a varied world distribution
scores.why: The most faithful member of the neural-CA family. Evolution (ES) stays the learner, and one continuous life is kept with no BPTT. Per-life world variation forces adaptation within the life, which suits generalisation and the mouse and text tasks. A noisy type vector copied at division gives emergent diversity without a type table. The cap-transfer metric (a rule evolved at cap 32 run at cap 128) is an explicit test of 'learn small, expand'. Send-on-delta messages restore event-driven, hardware-friendly communication. Weaknesses: ES in about 10k dimensions under Poisson F needs large populations. Adaptation lives in GRU state, not in durable inherited synapses. GRU cells are less readable than the GRN.

scores.name: Grow-and-Act NCA (GA-NCA): one shared neural rule per lattice site, trained by gradient through whole lives
scores.why: Size-agnostic shared rule; cell types emerge as attractors; polarity-relative messages give direction without the morphogen tax. Net2Net widening grows the rule's capacity without changing its function, and pool training keeps lives continuous. NCA growth and regeneration become visible within days, and gradients give dense credit assignment. Fidelity costs: gradient does the learning and evolution (PBT) only picks lineages. BPTT over 1k+ steps through a soft capture disk is the main risk to visible chasing. Messages are real-valued. Within-life learning happens only through slow channels. An MLP cell is harder to dissect. Hardware: an int8 MLP of about 4.7k MAC per step per tile, with the gap checked by the async gate.

scores.name: Logic tissue: evolved and differentiable gate-circuit cells that exchange spike bits, simulated bit-sliced
scores.why: The most hardware-native runtime: the evolved genome is the netlist, and a bit-exact simulator is the hardware, so there is no sim-to-hardware gap. Spikes stay as bits. CGP neutral drift is evolution-native. The measured 13-40x per-core speed-up gives fast, cheap iteration on a laptop. Pruned circuits can be read as Boolean rules. Fidelity costs: gates are less bio-like than membranes and genes, within-life learning is limited to state bits, graded integration costs many gates, and 500-gate netlists are hard to read unless pruned. Best used as the compile target for whatever rule wins.

scores.name: CellCode: LLM-guided evolution of the cell's event handlers (AlphaEvolve-style), checked by the exact clockless kernel
scores.why: Keeps every substrate preference. Integer handler programs are microcode for the planned cell processor, and charging per-event instructions as energy doubles as a cycle budget, so the hardware gap is zero. Its output is the most interpretable of all, readable code, which answers 'what local algorithms emerge' directly. Face-aware handlers make direction expressible. Islands plus MAP-Elites counter lineage collapse. It is cheap (about 24 CPU-h and $100 per seed, 2 weeks) and novel. Fidelity risk: the LLM's human prior writes designed roles, against minimal hard-coding. The AutoML-Zero control arm and the observable whitelist measure and limit this. The search operator itself is not bio-inspired.

scores.name: Vector-message tissue (NCA-style): a shared recurrent cell rule trained by gradients through development and behaviour, inside an evolutionary or PBT outer loop, grown by curriculum
scores.why: A near-duplicate of GA-NCA. Merge it, but keep its best parts: an occupied-cell gather representation (which also allows axon slots for arbitrary circuits), a three-arm design (BPTT vs ES vs warm start then ES), and the sim-to-clockless gate. It has the same fidelity costs as GA-NCA: gradient-led learning, real-valued messages, an opaque cell, and an MLP cell that is the weakest of these for FPGA tiles.

scores.name: Developmental graph tissue: cells that grow their own directed wires, with function-preserving division (NDP/LNDP-style)
scores.why: Strongest on arbitrary multidirectional circuitry (grown, pruned, length-paid directed wires), with exact Net2Net division and plasticity within the life. Bio-like (axon guidance), and the event-driven variant maps onto a network-on-chip. But the published evidence is small and modest (NDP did not solve LunarLander), edge growth needs degree caps (more hard-coding), and visible results come slower. Better added later as 'axon slots' on a lattice tissue.

scores.name: Logic tissue: differentiable-logic CA cells with binary spike messages, compiled to exact gates
scores.why: Duplicate of the bit-sliced logic tissue, with the same hardware strengths. Gradient-first DiffLogic training through a closed-loop world is unproven, and the authors report heavy tuning, so visible results are riskier. Its useful part, distilling a trained NCA rule into at most 2k gates, belongs in the merged logic-tissue track.

scores.name: Tensor spiking tissue on a GPU: ES at large population with antithetic common lives, evolved three-factor plasticity, and a gradient oracle
scores.why: Keeps LIF, GRN, spikes and life, and adds plasticity (overlaps Plastic faces). Its first two weeks are high-value diagnostics: the dt-equivalence curve, and a gradient oracle that says whether the gap is search or substrate. The full port costs 6-14 person-weeks for a 2-9x gain, which is poor value for visible outcomes. Keep the diagnostics; skip the full port.

scores.name: C. Predictive tissue: every cell minimises its own prediction error (a predictive-coding graph, optionally spike-coded on the two channels)
scores.why: Gives the inert hidden planes a job. Learning is local and Hebbian, works on arbitrary graphs, and inserting a zero-weight cell keeps function. It is bio-plausible and matches the prediction-heavy mouse and text tasks, and its week-1 test (a hidden plane predicting target position) is cheap and visible. But fast closed-loop control with PC is unproven: there are relaxation steps, the 'dark room' risk, and a fixed local objective that is hard-coded. Signed errors in spikes are awkward.

scores.name: Predictive tissue: every cell is a tiny local world model that learns during the life; evolution designs development and the learning rule (Baldwinian)
scores.why: Duplicate of predictive-coding candidate C. Merge them, keeping this version's better pieces: daughters inherit their mother's learned predictor (growth keeps learned function), send-on-delta event messages (event-driven runtime), and explicit Baldwin-effect measurements. Same risks: trivial predictors, misalignment with F, a fixed rule form.

scores.name: Open-ended world-body co-evolution with foundation-model curators (POET, OMNI-EPIC and ASAL around the existing substrate)
scores.why: Search-side only, so the substrate is untouched. It directly targets generalisation and lineage collapse. World axes such as field size and occlusion give growth and depth a reason to exist, so pressure to expand comes from the environment rather than a schedule. But it splits compute across worlds, transfers under Poisson noise are costly, and LLM-written worlds risk leaks. The cheap parametric v0 (a world distribution plus MAP-Elites) should be folded into the hybrid; the LLM world writer can come later.

scores.name: D. Differentiable twin for meta-plasticity: a gradient outer loop for rule parameters, evolution for development, the exact kernel as referee
scores.why: Excellent fidelity on the organism side: the organism is unchanged, and only the exact kernel's F selects. But gradients reach only the rule coefficients of frozen mature bodies, growth is not differentiated, the twin-kernel gap is unmeasured, and it overlaps the gradient oracle in Tensor spiking tissue. Use it as a diagnostic, not a direction.

scores.name: Learning tissue: two-stream cells that meta-learn a local learning rule (VSML/BLUR inside the NCA)
scores.why: The only design with true learning inside the life, through a backward channel and fast weights per face. New cells arrive able to learn, and fast weights are local registers on silicon. But meta-training is expensive and unstable, the result is the hardest of all to interpret, and visible outcomes are slow. It is an add-on once a base tissue works and worlds vary within a life.

scores.name: B. Meta-learned cell and synapse programs (a VSML-style tissue) trained on GPUs
scores.why: Duplicate of the VSML Learning tissue, overlapping the Shared in-context cell. A separate synapse program per face doubles state and ES meta-training cost. It is the only candidate where the learning algorithm itself is discovered, but it is black-box and its cost risk is high. Fold it into the in-context cell as an optional per-face fast-weight head.

scores.name: C. Organ duplication and divergence: modules as units, grown along a task ladder (dot, mouse, text)
scores.why: Duplication with divergence is bio-like and maps well onto the dot, mouse and text ladder and onto multi-core tiles. But module size and ports are hand-chosen, there is a clock inside each module (GALS), it drifts toward MoE engineering, and roles are less emergent. Its developmental form (duplicating a progenitor lineage, i.e. an organ) is worth keeping as a later mutation operator.

scores.name: D. Geometric genome with resolution growth: CPPN / ES-HyperNEAT with evolved local plasticity
scores.why: Weights become a global function of geometry, which is less emergent and biased toward regular patterns. It adds a second genome, and growth by upsampling preserves only spatially smooth computations. Its one useful insight, sign as a function of delta_z, is already delivered by polarity-relative or per-face plastic weights.

scores.name: B. Lamarckian morphing graphs: NEAT with function-preserving morphisms and a gradient/e-prop inner loop, tensorized on GPU
scores.why: Drops the developmental genetic code: the genome is a directly encoded network, not one genome that grows a tissue. It trains in lockstep over many episodes and is the least bio-like option. Its role as a 'best-case ML reference' is filled more cheaply by the gradient oracle on frozen bodies. Keep only its morphism operators (zero-init edges, split with outputs halved) as cross-cutting mutations.

judged.duplicates:
Clusters, with the representative to keep first.
(1) Shared neural rule per site on a GPU: Grow-and-Act NCA = Vector-message tissue (near-identical: gradient through life, PBT, curriculum, Net2Net). Shared in-context cell is the same substrate with ES and a world distribution in place of BPTT. Maturing tissue is that substrate plus per-edge plasticity and neutral division. Merge all four into one track with one ES arm and one BPTT warm-start arm.
(2) VSML-style learning tissue: 'Learning tissue (VSML/BLUR inside the NCA)' = 'B. Meta-learned cell and synapse programs'. Both become an optional fast-weight head on track (1).
(3) Logic tissue: 'differentiable-logic CA ... compiled to exact gates' = 'evolved and differentiable gate-circuit cells ... bit-sliced'. Keep the bit-sliced CGP version, with DiffLogic distillation as its warm start.
(4) Plasticity on the spiking substrate: 'A. Plastic faces' and the plasticity half of 'Tensor spiking tissue' are the same three-factor face rule. 'D. Differentiable twin' and the gradient oracle of 'Tensor spiking tissue' are the same diagnostic.
(5) Predictive tissue: 'C. Predictive tissue (PC graph)' = 'Predictive tissue (local world model, Baldwinian)'.
(6) Graphs with function-preserving division: 'Developmental graph tissue' overlaps 'Lamarckian morphing graphs' (both use Net2Net-split graphs). Only the former keeps development.
Cross-cutting ideas repeated in three or more angles, which should be treated as shared infrastructure rather than as candidates: Net2Net or zero-init growth; random update masks plus a clockless gate; ES with antithetic common random numbers; MAP-Elites, islands or QD against lineage collapse; daughters inheriting learned state; size curricula.
judged.missing:
1) Continuous-time cells that run under any update timing. Closed-form continuous-time (CfC/LTC) units (Hasani, Lechner, Amini, Liebenwein, Ray, Tschaikowski, Teschl, Rus 2021/2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.13898, opened) take the elapsed time as an input. A cell can therefore integrate exactly over its own interval since the last event, and the same rule runs in the GPU stepper and in the event-driven kernel. That closes the clock gap structurally instead of only testing it with random masks. Neural Circuit Policies (Lechner, Hasani, Amini, Henzinger, Rus, Grosu 2020, Nature Machine Intelligence, https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-020-00237-3; Crossref metadata only, full text not opened) are the small, sparse, bio-wired version for steering; that they steer a vehicle with very few neurons is my recollection, unverified.
2) Symbolic distillation of learned cell rules, so neural-cell candidates still answer 'what local algorithms emerge?'. Fit symbolic expressions to the trained message and update functions (Cranmer, Sanchez-Gonzalez, Battaglia, Xu, Cranmer, Spergel, Ho 2020, NeurIPS, https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11287, opened). The symbolic form is also a compact rule to put in hardware, an alternative to logic-gate compilation.
3) A privileged teacher with a local student. Train a non-local policy that sees the true target (cheap), then train the tissue to imitate its per-act-cell actions with dense, noise-free supervision. Finish with ES on true F (Chen, Zhou, Koltun, Krähenbühl 2019, Learning by Cheating, CoRL, https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.12294, opened). This is the fastest route to visible chasing, and a cheaper 'substrate or search?' oracle than BPTT through whole lives.
4) Cells as the body itself: voxel-based soft robots with a controller distributed per voxel. Growth then changes morphology, and locomotion and regeneration are directly visible and measurable (Medvet, Bartoli, De Lorenzo, Fidel 2020, GECCO, https://doi.org/10.1145/3377930.3390173, Crossref metadata only; Bhatia, Jackson, Tian, Xu, Matusik 2021, Evolution Gym, NeurIPS, https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09863, opened). Only Horibe 2021 touched this.
5) Give apoptosis a job explicitly. Continual-learning work (Dohare 2024, cited by the plasticity angle) re-initialises low-utility units, and in the tissue that would be death of low-eligibility cells followed by regrowth. Only one cross-cutting note raised it, and no candidate builds it in, although p_die is unused in every evolved body.
6) Tooling for visible outcomes: a live viewer streaming batched GPU lives (growth, chasing, lesion and regrowth) so every run is watchable. It is cheap and it shortens the iteration loop more than any substrate change.
7) Warm-start any new substrate from the existing evolved genomes, porting s5 and s4 as fixed rules or distillation targets, so new paradigms start at the pilot's level rather than at zero (touched only as fidelity checks).
judged.best_hybrid:
'Plastic maturing tissue'. Merge Plastic faces A, Maturing tissue, Shared in-context cell and GA-NCA, then compile the result into the logic tissue.

PHASE 0 (days, current C kernel, laptop or one spot box):
(a) The hand-set 'timing teaches direction' STDP test on s5 with chemistry knocked out (under 1 CPU-h).
(b) Function-preserving gene duplication: copy the gene's row, halve its outgoing weights, and report a 'birth deficit' readout.
(c) Antithetic ES with common random numbers (CRN) against the GA at equal lives.
These produce the first visible answers, and nothing in the organism changes.

PHASE 1 (2-3 weeks, one rented L4 or 4090, torch). Build one shared cell rule on the hex-prism lattice.
- Cell: a small recurrent state (GRN-form or CfC, 16-32 values, int8-friendly). It should not be GRU and GRN together.
- Messages: per-face messages of 1-2 spike bits, with at most a 4-value int8 variant as an arm.
- Plasticity: per-face plastic weights plus eligibility traces, under an evolved three-factor rule. The modulator is released locally by the cell that senses a capture.
- Division: daughters copy the learned face table, a noisy type vector and their state, and enter through a fade-in output gain, so division is neutral.
- Direction: polarity-relative faces instead of morphogen gradients.
- Search: ES with CRN over a world distribution drawn per life (target speed, receptor-sign flip, occluder, later mouse traces), with MAP-Elites niches. An optional BPTT or privileged-teacher warm start is used for pretraining only. Selection always uses true Poisson F.
- Gates, all visible: birth deficit about 0; cap transfer (a rule from cap 32 keeps F at cap 128); freezing plasticity mid-life costs F; recovery after a sign flip; lateral_off still removes more than 50% of F; at least 80-90% of F under unseen update masks and delays, then in an exact event-driven re-run.

PHASE 2: compile the winner to the integer ABI and distil it into the bit-sliced logic tissue, which is the hardware artefact with no sim-to-hardware gap. Extract symbolic rules for interpretation. Run CellCode in parallel on the C kernel as a cheap second track, because its output is readable and native to the kernel.

judged.judge:
Lens: hardware-native rollouts first, training compute second, with heavy weight on cheap, fast, visible outcomes (per the user's follow-up).

What I checked:
- docs/HARDWARE_PATH.md:
  - Today's GRN+LIF tile costs about 0.3-1.6 nJ per cell per model unit [E].
  - GRN ticks are 65-87% of that.
  - The genome copy is about 9x a cell's own state.
  - Lockstep dt is "acceptable only as a declared approximation".
- The prior synthesis in scratchpad/alt/alternatives.md.
- The two stand-in benchmarks. hardware/bitslice3.c is a random 512-gate netlist on a ring of 300 sites. It has no hex routing, no world, no receptor sampling and no growth bookkeeping, so the 13-40x per-core gain is an upper bound until the world is added.

How I scored:
1. **Cost of one unit-step on silicon.** Gates and bits beat an integer GRN, which beats an int8 MLP or GRU. Per-face synapse GRUs are worst. Rough orders [E, not verified]:
   - a 1k-gate logic cell: about pJ per step;
   - an int8 MLP with about 5k MAC: about nJ per step, plus weight fetch;
   - today's GRN tile: 0.3-1.6 nJ per model unit.
2. **The sim-to-hardware gap**, which can come from:
   - float to int;
   - sync to async;
   - a relaxed versus hardened rule;
   - a soft versus hard capture disk;
   - a twin dt.
3. **Whether growth and within-life learning run on the tile fabric**, rather than only between generations.
4. **Time to a visible body or behaviour on a laptop or one GPU.**
5. **Engineering cost from the C kernel, torch and probe tooling.**

The verdict:
- **Logic tissue wins on the primary lens.** The evolved netlist is the hardware, the bit-sliced simulator is bit-exact to RTL, and it is also the cheapest per life on a CPU.
- **Plastic faces and CellCode come next.** Their organism is the exact integer, event-driven kernel, so the gap is zero. They give the fastest visible results: the STDP direction test takes hours.
- **NCA and GRU cells are good GPU training vehicles but heavy silicon.** They are best used as teachers to distil into gates.
- **VSML synapse programs, NEAT morphing graphs and CPPNs score low.** Each is heavy per site, has no growth inside the life, or puts a global-looking generator into the runtime.

Verification: I checked the four citations I add, in "missing", through Crossref metadata only, not full text. My Crossref check of DWN returned 429, so I rely on the hardware angle's citation for it.

scores.name: Logic tissue: evolved and differentiable gate-circuit cells that exchange spike bits, simulated bit-sliced
scores.why:
**Best fit to the primary lens.**
- **The cell is the hardware.** It is a netlist of a few hundred to 1k 2-input gates plus 16-64 state bits, with bounded fan-in (8 faces x 2 bits) and no multipliers. It maps straight to LUT6s or standard cells, at roughly pJ per step against nJ for the GRN tile [E].
- **The simulator is the RTL.** Bit-sliced C is bit-exact to the netlist, so the only remaining gap is timing. That gap can be closed exactly (see 'missing': LFSR-driven update enables, or handshake semantics).

**Training is cheap and visible.**
- Measured 2.6-7.6 ms per life on one laptop core [M, stand-in]. 64-256 lives per word give common random numbers for free.
- CGP needs no differentiable world, so the first evolved body could be about 1 week of engine work plus a laptop-day.
- yosys gives LUT counts the same day.

**Risks.**
- The stand-in excludes the per-lane world and receptor sampling, and the 20-25% occupancy waste of a dense box.
- CGP is slow on large circuits.
- No published logic CA steers a body.

scores.name: Logic tissue: differentiable-logic CA cells with binary spike messages, compiled to exact gates
scores.why:
**Same end artefact as the bit-sliced logic tissue, so merge them.**
- Hardware nativeness is equal: hardened gates, spike bits, async masks.
- It scores one point lower because its main route is gradient-first: relaxed DiffLogic trained by BPTT through a torch SPECK port with a soft capture. That adds a relaxed-to-hard gap and a long-horizon training risk the authors themselves flag ('extensive hyperparameter tuning'), and pushes the first visible body to weeks 2-3.

**Its unique value.**
- Distilling the hand reflex, the router and s5 probe traces, or an NCA teacher, into gates. That is a cheap early visible result: a gate-level reflex body chasing in the viewer.
- Pass-through-gate growth that preserves function.

scores.name: A. Plastic faces: evolved three-factor STDP on per-face synapses, inherited at division (keeps the clockless kernel)
scores.why:
**Zero sim-to-hardware gap.** The organism is the exact event-driven integer-ABI kernel.
- Trace-based three-factor learning is what on-chip learning silicon implements (Loihi, ReckOn).
- About 50 extra Q8/Q16 numbers per cell, receiver-local, window-scheduler exact.

**Fastest visible outcome of all 19.** The STDP direction test needs no evolution and under 1 CPU-h: knock out s5's chemistry, switch on hand-set STDP, run 256 paired lives. A full matrix is about 5 h on one 192-core box.

**Held back from top marks.**
- The tile is still the GRN tile (0.3-1.6 nJ per cell per unit [E]), far heavier than a gate cell.
- It gains no training throughput.

**Bonus.** If STDP works, the same rule can be built into the logic cell as per-face enable or counter bits.

scores.name: CellCode: LLM-guided evolution of the cell's event handlers (AlphaEvolve-style), checked by the exact clockless kernel
scores.why:
**Runtime.** Integer C with bounded loops, run by the exact clockless kernel, with a whitelist of local observables and the instruction count charged as energy. That makes the evolved program microcode for a per-tile core, or HLS input, and the per-event cycle budget is explicit.
- No sim-to-hardware gap.
- A small core per tile is bigger than a 1k-gate cell, which is why it ranks below logic tissue.

**Outer loop.** An LLM over an API plus about 15 CPU-h; nothing to port.

**Visible results.** About 2 weeks, and the evolved algorithm is readable, with probe reports feeding back into the prompt.

**Risks.**
- The LLM's human priors run against minimal hard-coding; an AutoML-Zero control arm measures that.
- Poisson noise remains.

**Can also write** the plasticity rule (candidate 5) or the gate netlist (candidate 13).

scores.name: Grow-and-Act NCA (GA-NCA): one shared neural rule per lattice site, trained by gradient through whole lives
scores.why:
**Rollout.** The trained cell is an int8 MLP of about 4.7k MAC per site per step, times several micro-steps per world unit. That needs a MAC array per tile, roughly GRN-tile energy or more [E].

**Gaps to close.**
- float to int8;
- synchronous training to asynchronous hardware;
- soft capture in training versus the hard Poisson disk at test.

**Training.** The training story is the strongest: gradients, PBT and GPU batching, with NCA growth visible within hours. But a torch SPECK port plus long-horizon BPTT comes before the first chase, and it is 222 ms per life on CPU [M].

**Under this lens:** keep it as a GPU teacher to distil into logic tissue, not as the organism.

scores.name: Tensor spiking tissue on a GPU: ES at large population with antithetic common lives, evolved three-factor plasticity, and a gradient oracle
scores.why:
**The organism is native** (same as Plastic faces), but the GPU part fails the lens.
- A 6-14 person-week port for 2-9x per dollar, on a stepped twin whose dt equivalence is unmeasured. That is training fidelity risk with no rollout gain.

**Pieces worth extracting.**
- Antithetic ES with common random numbers on today's CPU kernel (days).
- The dt-equivalence measurement.
- The gradient oracle on frozen bodies.

**Drop the full GPU port** unless the oracle says search is the bottleneck and CPU ES is too slow.

scores.name: D. Differentiable twin for meta-plasticity: a gradient outer loop for rule parameters, evolution for development, the exact kernel as referee
scores.why:
**The organism keeps every hardware property**: the exact kernel decides, and plastic LIF is native.

**But it builds and maintains a second (twin) simulator**, and gains only appear if:
- the twin-kernel F gap over dt is small (unmeasured);
- surrogate gradients survive 1,000+ spiking steps.

**Visible results** take weeks, and it overlaps the tensor-tissue oracle. Worth doing only if candidate 5 plus ES stalls on search.

scores.name: Maturing tissue: GPU neural-CA cells with neutral division and evolved plasticity
scores.why:
**Same heavy NCA tile as GA-NCA**, plus per-edge weights and traces, so more state per tile.
- Lockstep GPU training, with replay in the event-driven kernel only for a spiking variant.

**Its two best ideas are cheap and portable** to any substrate, including the logic and plastic tissues:
- silent-newborn fade-in, which preserves function;
- the 'birth deficit' readout.

**As a standalone candidate:** merge into the NCA family.

scores.name: Vector-message tissue (NCA-style): a shared recurrent cell rule trained by gradients through development and behaviour, inside an evolutionary or PBT outer loop, grown by curriculum
scores.why:
**A duplicate of GA-NCA.** Its own angle rates it the weakest of three for FPGA/ASIC: thousands of MACs per update, so time-multiplexed MAC arrays rather than a tile per cell.

**Measured** 0.31-0.67 CPU-s per life [M]; GPU gains are estimates only.

**Useful additions:**
- an occupied-cell list plus a neighbour table, which avoids empty-site waste and allows long edges;
- the explicit plan to distil into logic.

scores.name: Shared in-context cell on GPU: one meta-learned recurrent rule in every cell, vector messages, evolution strategies over a varied world distribution
scores.why:
**A duplicate of the NCA family**, with ES in place of BPTT.

**Runtime.** A GRU of 2-20k parameters per site is a heavy tile. EGRU send-on-delta helps energy but not area.

**Training.** ES in about 10k dimensions on Poisson F is sample-hungry, and the JAX port is 2-3 weeks before any visible result.

**Keep these ideas:**
- worlds drawn per life;
- the cap-transfer metric.

Fold them into whichever substrate wins.

scores.name: Predictive tissue: every cell is a tiny local world model that learns during the life; evolution designs development and the learning rule (Baldwinian)
scores.why:
**Hardware.** Local outer-product updates are chip-friendly, and its send-on-delta error events can stay event-driven in the C kernel, slightly more native than the plasticity-angle version.

**Against it.**
- Graded payloads.
- A per-cell predictor of 100-500 weights.
- An unproven link from prediction to action.
- Little to gain in reactive SPECK.

**Best kept for** the cursor and text worlds. A duplicate of the plasticity angle's predictive tissue.

scores.name: C. Predictive tissue: every cell minimises its own prediction error (a predictive-coding graph, optionally spike-coded on the two channels)
Developmental graph tissue: cells that grow their own directed wires, with function-preserving division (NDP/LNDP-style)
scores.why:
**Its value.** It is the only route to long-range circuits without relay chains, and the event-driven variant maps onto a SpiNNaker-style network-on-chip.

**Runtime costs on silicon.**
- Wiring by query/key top-k over a radius, plus per-node GRUs and per-edge plasticity, needs programmable routing tables that are rewritten during life.
- Edges must be allocated dynamically, with degree caps.
- Gather/scatter is inefficient on GPU.

**Evidence is small:** under 100 nodes; LunarLander not solved.

**Keep as later 'axon slots'** on top of a winning lattice cell.

scores.name: Open-ended world-body co-evolution with foundation-model curators (POET, OMNI-EPIC and ASAL around the existing substrate)
scores.why:
**Neutral on the primary lens**: it changes no runtime and inherits the substrate's hardware story.

**Pros.** The parametric v0 is CPU-only and cheap, and it attacks lineage collapse and generalisation.

**Cons.** It splits compute across worlds, and visible gains are indirect. LLM-written worlds need a World ABI linter.

**Add later** as a wrapper around the logic or plastic tissue.

scores.name: C. Organ duplication and divergence: modules as units, grown along a task ladder (dot, mouse, text)
D. Geometric genome with resolution growth: CPPN / ES-HyperNEAT with evolved local plasticity
scores.why:
**Two bad options at runtime:**
- precompute the weights, giving a fixed network that cannot grow on chip;
- run a CPPN MLP per synapse query at every growth event, which costs many MACs per new edge.

**Also against it:**
- it moves decisions into a geometry function, reducing cell-level emergence;
- the key claim, zero-shot transfer across resolution, could not be verified by its own author.

**Cheap GPU training does not offset the rollout cost.**

scores.name: Meta-learned cell and synapse programs (a VSML-style tissue) trained on GPUs
scores.why:
**Heaviest runtime of the set.**
- A cell GRU plus a synapse GRU on each of 8 faces per site per step: thousands of MACs plus per-face state RAM.
- Wider-than-spike links.

**Training.** Meta-training by ES over 1,000-step unrolls is the costliest outer loop here.

**First visible result** is a 19-site sign-flip demo after about 3 weeks. Interesting science, wrong lens.

scores.name: Learning tissue: two-stream cells that meta-learn a local learning rule (VSML/BLUR inside the NCA)
scores.why:
**A duplicate of the VSML-style tissue, placed on top of the NCA:** about 2-3x the NCA tile cost, and the NCA tile is already heavy.

**Nested meta-training** with BPTT over lifetimes is unstable and expensive.

**Depends on candidate 1 existing first**, so the first visible result is week 3 or later. Revisit only after a winning substrate exists and the worlds vary within a life.

scores.name: B. Lamarckian morphing graphs: NEAT with function-preserving morphisms and a gradient/e-prop inner loop, tensorized on GPU
scores.why:
**Fails the runtime criterion.**
- No growth inside the life: the organism is a fixed direct-encoded graph.
- It drops the developmental genome.
- It trains in lockstep with BPTT and proxy losses.

**A trained sparse SNN does map well to neuromorphic chips**, but that is ordinary SNN deployment, not a grown tissue.

**Useful only as a 'best-case ML' reference arm.** The morphism operators (zero-init edges, split nodes) should be kept as cross-cutting tools.

judged.missing:
1. **A stepped rule does not need a global clock in silicon.** Every angle treats "trained in steps" as clock-dependent and then tests timing tolerance statistically. A synchronous CA rule can instead run exactly on clockless or GALS hardware through local handshakes: a tile computes step k once its neighbours' step k-1 outputs have arrived.
   - **Theory:** Nehaniv 2004, "Asynchronous Automata Networks Can Emulate Any Synchronous Automata Network", Int. J. Algebra and Computation, https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218196704002043. Crossref metadata only.
   - **Circuit form:** the bundled-data handshake of Sutherland's "Micropipelines" (Turing lecture 1989; Crossref lists the 2007 ACM Turing Award Lectures reprint, https://doi.org/10.1145/1283920.1283946). Metadata only.
   - **Consequence:** a logic tissue can be bit-exact on asynchronous silicon, with zero sim-to-hardware gap. The random-mask "async gate" then tests biological robustness, not whether the rule can be built.

2. **Make the training-time asynchrony reproducible in silicon.** Drive each tile's update-enable bit from a per-tile LFSR seeded by its position. The update mask used in training is then reproduced bit for bit on the FPGA or ASIC, so "random" asynchrony adds no sim-to-hardware gap.

3. **Evolve against the bit-exact digital model, and put the result on a physical board early.**
   - **The physical demo.** No candidate puts the organism on hardware. An ECP5 or iCE40 board with the open yosys/nextpnr flow could run the synthesised logic tissue with the dot world in fabric or on a soft core, driving a VGA/HDMI dot-chase or a real mouse. That is the most visible possible outcome and is directly on the user's hardware goal.
   - **Tiny Tapeout is the next step.** HARDWARE_PATH quotes about EUR 70 per tile.
   - **Precedents:**
     - Embryonics: cell-based, genome-carrying, self-repairing FPGA tissues. Mange, Sipper, Stauffer & Tempesti 2000, Proc. IEEE 88(4), https://doi.org/10.1109/5.842998. Metadata only.
     - The cautionary tale: evolution run on a real FPGA exploited analog physics. Thompson 1997, "An evolved circuit, intrinsic in silicon, entwined with physics", LNCS, https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-63173-9_61. Metadata only.
     - Together these support the user's split: evolve off-chip against the exact digital model, and run rollouts on-chip.

4. **Train under integer or bit semantics from day one** instead of float-then-quantise. For any NCA or GRU arm, use int8 weights, int16 state, shift-based leaks and int32 accumulation in torch integer tensors, searched by ES (EGGROLL already handles integer-only recurrent models). The GPU simulator then equals the RTL, and there is no QAT gap.

5. **LUT cells** (weightless or LUT networks such as DWN, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11112, cited by the hardware angle; my own check of it was rate-limited) as an alternative to 2-input gates. k-input tables map 1:1 onto FPGA LUT6s, with fewer layers per step.

6. **Hardware cost as part of fitness, in hardware units.** Charge gate toggles, messages and gate count per step against an area cap, not only abstract energy. A frozen shared rule can also be hardwired, so it needs no per-cell genome storage. That matters because HARDWARE_PATH found the genome copy dominates tile area.

7. **Compile today's best bodies first.** Distil the hand reflex, the router (+2.25 F over the reflex in the same substrate) and s4/s5 into gates or programs. This gives a hardware-native body that already chases, before any search. It is the cheapest visible result on the new substrate, and it tells you how many gates each known algorithm needs.
judged.best_hybrid:
**Bit-exact logic tissue, with STDP-as-bits and a distillation warm start.**

**Day 1, in the existing kernel: the STDP direction test from Plastic faces.**
- Switch off s5's chemical direction (a_c = 0), turn on hand-set trace STDP, and run 256 paired common-random-number lives (under 1 CPU-h).
- It answers whether timing alone builds "excite from below, inhibit from above".
- Whatever the answer, it decides whether the logic cell needs per-face plasticity bits.

**Week 1: the engine.** A bit-sliced C engine on the hex-prism lattice, with:
- alive, divide and die bits, and random-priority claims for division;
- 2 spike bits per face, and delay lines of 1-3 steps;
- the dot world and receptor pings per lane, sampled by skipping between events;
- 64-256 common-random-number lives per word;
- per-tile LFSR update enables, so the "asynchronous" schedule is exactly reproducible in hardware.

Measure lives/s per core with the world included. That replaces the stand-in's 2.6-7.6 ms per life.

**Week 1-2: the first visible bodies.** Distil the hand reflex, the router and s4/s5 probe I/O into netlists, using difflogic in torch on small traces, or by hand. These are hardware-native bodies that chase from the start, and the distillation shows how many gates each algorithm costs.

**Weeks 2-3: CGP evolution.** Evolve CGP netlists of at most 512-1,000 gates, seeded from the distilled bodies.
- **Mutation and growth:** neutral drift through inactive genes, and pass-through-gate growth that preserves function.
- **Diversity:** islands or MAP-Elites, with descriptors such as lateral share, size and growth-stop time.
- **Selection** on the real Poisson F, with common random numbers built into the bit lanes.
- **Plasticity, if Day 1 succeeded:** add per-face enable or counter bits that implement 1-bit STDP. "Learn small, keep it on division" then becomes state bits copied into daughters.

**Week 4: the hardware.** Synthesise the best cell with yosys and abc (LUT count, gate toggles per step). Put a small tissue plus the world on a cheap ECP5 board as a physical demo, using handshake or LFSR-enable semantics so it matches the simulator bit for bit.

**Fallbacks.**
- If CGP stalls, train a GA-NCA on one rented GPU as a teacher and distil it into gates.
- CellCode, writing the netlist or a per-event program with an LLM, is the alternative structural mutator.

**Success criteria.**
- At least 20x more lives per core than the current kernel, with the world included.
- A gate body at or above reflex@hollow3, or at least s5's level, within one laptop-day of evolution.
- At most about 1-3k LUT6 per cell.
- F within 10% across update-enable densities 0.3-0.7.
- Board output bit-identical to the simulator.

judged.judge:
Lens: compute efficiency to visible outcomes. I asked of each candidate: what is the expected watchable progress (growth, chasing, regrowth after damage, adaptation mid-life) per GPU-day and per engineering-week, and what is the risk that nothing visible appears? The binding clarification applies throughout: the organism's runtime must map natively onto hardware. The outer loop may use any machinery.

Grounding:
- Read RESULTS.md, including the compute audit (0.07-0.15 CPU-s per life, 24 CPU-h per run, about $6-16 per pilot on a rented 192-core box).
- There is no GPU on this machine (nvidia-smi is absent; 14 CPU threads).
- The repo already has a batched, stepped torch tissue with a GIF writer: src/develop.py (batched GRN development, morphogen diffusion, division claims), src/cells.py (quantised stepped LIF) and src/render.py (PIL GIFs). The one-life C kernel also has probe.py and the atlas viewer.
- New measurement [M]: forward plus backward through a 2-plane 11x11 hex NCA (242 sites, 1.9k params, 64 lives, 32-step window, 8 threads) costs 89 us per trained life-step on this laptop CPU, i.e. 183 ms per update. A Growing-NCA-scale training run (about 10k updates) is therefore about 30 min on the laptop, so the first watchable NCA result needs no GPU at all. Script: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jgon-project-ml-cell-dev/aefb0c66-3af5-49c4-936c-154d6434706c/scratchpad/alt/judge_compute/tiny_bptt.py.
- One new citation, opened: Xu, Makoviychuk, Narang, Ramos, Matusik, Garg, Macklin (2022, ICLR), Accelerated Policy Learning with Parallel Differentiable Simulation (SHAC), https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.07137. It reports more than 17x less training time on muscle-actuated locomotion.
- I also opened Evolution Gym (Bhatia, Jackson, Tian, Xu, Matusik; NeurIPS 2021; https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09863). It is not used: it is a CPU co-design benchmark without growth within a life.
- GPU prices are not re-checked; everything about the GPU is an estimate.

Main conclusion: the dense shared-rule NCA family wins on this lens. Three things put it ahead:
- Gradients give a direction in about 5k dimensions from every batch of lives.
- Engines and training recipes for growth and regrowth already exist and are known to work.
- Each experiment runs in minutes, at small scale on the laptop.

Evolution-only candidates have to fight Poisson selection noise and stay slow, whatever their hardware fit. The logic tissue is the best runtime but a poor first trainer, so it should be the compile target.

scores.name: Grow-and-Act NCA (GA-NCA): one shared neural rule per lattice site, trained by gradient through whole lives
scores.why:
Fastest route to watchable results.
- Growth plus regrowth on the hex prism: hours on the laptop CPU ($0; 89 us per trained life-step [M]). This is a known-good recipe (Growing NCA) that also validates the engine and the async mask.
- A chasing body: about 1-2 engineering-weeks (a stepped torch SPECK port; src/develop.py and render.py can be reused), plus 10-50 GPU-h on a rented L4 or 4090, roughly $20-100 [E].
- Iteration: minutes per experiment at small R_cap.
- Gradients beat GA sample efficiency by orders of magnitude for the continuous part.

Risks:
- Long-horizon BPTT and the soft-capture proxy. Mitigate with pool windows plus a SHAC-style critic, and keep the Poisson world as the judge.
- Lockstep artefacts, caught by the async gate.

Hardware: an int8 MLP per tile, fan-in 8, local. Native enough if trained with update masks, delay jitter and quantisation-aware training (QAT) from day 1. It is also the teacher for logic compilation.

The port check (encode the hand reflex as a fixed rule and match the kernel's F) is exactly the right first gate.

scores.name: Vector-message tissue (NCA-style): a shared recurrent cell rule trained by gradients through development and behaviour, inside an evolutionary or PBT outer loop, grown by curriculum
scores.why:
Essentially the same substrate as GA-NCA, with two useful additions:
- an occupied-cell gather representation, which skips the 75-80% of empty sites and gives axon slots for free;
- explicit BPTT, ES and warm-start-then-ES arms.

Compute:
- Its measured CPU cost (0.31-0.67 s per 4,096-step life) agrees with my measurement, so debugging on the laptop is fine.
- A rented L4 or 4090 for a few days is under about $100 [E].

Time to a visible result is the same as GA-NCA: growth in a day, chase in 2-3 weeks. It scores slightly lower because 'fuse the whole life into one kernel' and the JAX/torch fork are extra engineering before anything is visible, and there is no port-fidelity check against the reflex.

Hardware: same as GA-NCA. It names distillation into logic as the path, which is right. Merge it with GA-NCA.

scores.name: Shared in-context cell on GPU: one meta-learned recurrent rule in every cell, vector messages, evolution strategies over a varied world distribution
scores.why:
The ES twin of GA-NCA. Strengths:
- Fitness is the true F with one continuous life: no soft disk, no BPTT memory, and discrete growth is handled naturally.
- Antithetic pairs with common random numbers average the Poisson noise that cripples the GA.
- Varied worlds per life make within-life adaptation (a sensor flip mid-life) a visible outcome.

Cost:
- 2-3 weeks of engineering for the JAX port, plus 2-3 L4/A100-days ($30-150 [E]) to a first chase.
- Each ES generation takes seconds to tens of seconds [E].
- Iteration is slower than BPTT (an ES gradient needs about 10^3 lives), and it is riskier from a cold start in about 10k dimensions.

Best used as the judge-aligned fine-tuner after a gradient or behavioural-cloning warm start. Hardware: an int8 GRU per tile with send-on-delta messages, native.

scores.name: Maturing tissue: GPU neural-CA cells with neutral division and evolved plasticity
scores.why:
A merger of GA-NCA, plastic faces and ES. The parts are good: silent newborns fading in, the birth-deficit metric, and per-face weights without chemistry.

Under this lens it has too many moving parts for a first watchable result:
- The GRN is kept alongside a GRU.
- There is a three-factor rule and maturation gains.
- ES runs over all of it.

The estimate (<$100, one L4 for days) is fine, but 3 weeks of engineering before the first chase, and plasticity adding a second failure mode, lower the expected visible progress per week.

Fold its neutral-division and birth-deficit measurements into the GA-NCA build as week-3 add-ons. Hardware is fine (local MAC plus trace per face).

scores.name: A. Plastic faces: evolved three-factor STDP on per-face synapses, inherited at division (keeps the clockless kernel)
scores.why:
The cheapest decisive experiment of the whole set.
- After about 1-1.5 engineering-weeks of kernel work (a reference.py twin, golden tests showing ABI-3 behaviour is bitwise unchanged at zero coefficients), the hand-set STDP test on s5 with chemical direction knocked out costs under 1 CPU-h.
- It reuses probe.py and the atlas viewer, so the result is watchable at once: per-face weight maps forming.
- The full matrix is about 720-940 CPU-h, about $15-35 spot.

Hardware: zero sim-to-hardware gap, since the exact kernel is the reference and trace learning is Loihi/ReckOn-native.

Why not higher: it stays inside the slow, noisy GA regime (about 0.005 F per generation late in a run), so beyond the STDP test, visible progress per CPU-day is incremental. Plasticity may also go unused unless worlds change within a life. Run it as the parallel CPU track, not the main bet.

scores.name: Logic tissue: differentiable-logic CA cells with binary spike messages, compiled to exact gates
scores.why:
Best runtime of all 19:
- The hardened netlist is the hardware.
- It is bit-exact, with value-less spikes.
- Bit-sliced CPU evaluation is 21.6 ms per life [M], against about 100 ms for today's kernel.

As a first trainer it is poor:
- The DiffLogic CA authors report heavy hyperparameter tuning even for static patterns.
- No closed-loop control or growth-plus-behaviour result exists.
- Relaxed-to-hard gaps appear over long horizons.

Visible first result: reproducing DiffLogic lizard-style growth on the hex prism takes days on CPU or GPU and is cheap. A chasing logic body from scratch has a high risk of nothing visible.

Shortlisted as stage 2: distil a trained NCA's per-cell I/O into at most 2k gates, then harden, then refine by CGP in a bit-sliced asynchronous referee. That closes the sim-to-hardware gap the NCA leaves open.

scores.name: Logic tissue: evolved and differentiable gate-circuit cells that exchange spike bits, simulated bit-sliced
scores.why:
A duplicate of the DiffLogic logic tissue with the evolution-first emphasis.

Strong points:
- Measured 2.6-7.6 ms per life on one core (13-40x faster than the kernel) [M, stand-in without world or growth].
- 64-256 common-random-number lives come free per word, so noise averaging is nearly free.
- No GPU rental is needed.

Weak points under this lens:
- 1-2 weeks to build a bit-sliced engine with the world per lane and growth bookkeeping before anything is visible.
- CGP on a closed-loop task with Poisson fitness is still mutation-plus-selection, with the same destructive-child problem (about -0.19 F per child).
- Risk of nothing beyond the SPECK median within a laptop-day is moderate to high.

Its engine is the right asynchronous referee and runtime for the distilled logic tissue. Build it as that, not as the primary search.

scores.name: Tensor spiking tissue on a GPU: ES at large population with antithetic common lives, evolved three-factor plasticity, and a gradient oracle
scores.why:
High diagnostic value, low visible value.
- Week 1: a stepped torch replay of frozen grown bodies and a dt sweep against the kernel. About a week, $0-50, and a real deliverable.
- Then the gradient oracle, which answers 'search or substrate?'.

But:
- GPU gain per dollar is only 2-9x (the repo's own estimate).
- A full port is 6-14 person-weeks.
- Its outcomes are mostly numbers, not new behaviour.

The cheapest piece, ES with common random numbers on the existing CPU kernel, needs days, no rental, and shows up in the existing atlas. It should be done regardless; I put it in the hybrid's CPU track.

Hardware: excellent (LIF plus eligibility traces as on ReckOn; fixed point is fitness-neutral).

scores.name: CellCode: LLM-guided evolution of the cell's event handlers (AlphaEvolve-style), checked by the exact clockless kernel
scores.why:
Cheap and fully reusing:
- Exact kernel, probe.py and atlas.
- About 15 CPU-h per seed, plus $10-300 of LLM calls [E].
- 2 weeks of engineering (linter, compile per candidate, OpenEvolve hook).
- Bodies are watchable in the existing viewer immediately.
- Hardware: zero gap; the evolved program is integer microcode with a cycle budget.

Under this lens the visible progress is uncertain:
- Noisy F (per-life reliability 0.026) makes LLM reflection unreliable.
- 'Beats the reflex' may just mean the LLM wrote the reflex, which defeats minimal hard-coding.
- Large semantic edits help only if they are not mostly destructive, which is unmeasured.

Worth a 1-week time-boxed pilot with the AutoML-Zero control arm, not a main track.

scores.name: D. Differentiable twin for meta-plasticity: a gradient outer loop for rule parameters, evolution for development, the exact kernel as referee
scores.why:
It overlaps the tensor-spiking oracle (the twin of frozen bodies plus a dt sweep), with an added gradient search for plasticity coefficients.
- A JAX twin of LIF, GRN and morphogens is a substantial port.
- BPTT through spiking dynamics over more than 1,000 steps is fragile.
- It produces calibrated numbers rather than new behaviour.

Visible progress per week is low. Keep only its week-1 dt-versus-F curve, which is useful, and merge that into the tensor-spiking diagnostic.

Hardware: kept native, because the exact kernel stays the referee.

scores.name: B. Lamarckian morphing graphs: NEAT with function-preserving morphisms and a gradient/e-prop inner loop, tensorized on GPU
scores.why:
Cost: 2-3 weeks of engineering and 2-4 GPU-days.

It would show a recurrent graph steering a dot, but no visible growth or regrowth of a body, because development is dropped. It is mainly a 'best-case ML' ceiling. A much cheaper ceiling (PPO or ES on a fixed small RNN in the ported world, in hours) gives the same calibration.

Risks:
- Morphisms are only approximately function-preserving for LIF.
- A proxy loss is needed for the inner loop.
- Lamarckian inheritance can hasten lineage collapse.

Hardware: sparse SNN, neuromorphic-friendly, but with a direct encoding. Keep the idea of morphism mutations; skip the system.

scores.name: Developmental graph tissue: cells that grow their own directed wires, with function-preserving division (NDP/LNDP-style)
scores.why:
Costs and limits:
- Engineering: gather/scatter edges, wire seeking, Net2Net division, degree caps.
- Search: ES in about 5k dimensions, likely 3+ weeks before a chase.
- Evidence: modest and small-scale (the NDP did not solve LunarLander).
- Viewing: edge graphs are harder to watch than tissue.

The risk that nothing visible emerges is high. Its genuine value is long-range wiring against the per-cell cost of relaying, which can be added later as K axon slots in the gather-based NCA instead of a separate paradigm.

Hardware: radius-bounded edges map onto a network-on-chip. Fine.

scores.name: Learning tissue: two-stream cells that meta-learn a local learning rule (VSML/BLUR inside the NCA)
scores.why: Within-life learning is very watchable (catching recovers after a sign flip), but meta-training is the most expensive and least stable loop here, and it depends on the NCA base existing first. Expect weeks 3-6 and tens to hundreds of GPU-h before a clean learning curve [E], with a real risk that the outer loop ignores the learner. Add it to the NCA once the base chases; per-face fast-weight registers keep the runtime native.

scores.name: B. Meta-learned cell and synapse programs (a VSML-style tissue) trained on GPUs
scores.why: It duplicates the shared in-context cell (ES on GPU) and the VSML learning tissue, while adding a second recurrent program per contact and meta-training over a task family. That means more parameters, higher ES variance, $100-300 [E] and a harder-to-read black box, all before the first visible result. Its useful pieces (synapse state copied at division, type genes) can be added to the shared in-context cell later.

scores.name: Open-ended world-body co-evolution with foundation-model curators (POET, OMNI-EPIC and ASAL around the existing substrate)
scores.why:
v0 (parametric POET over CATCH settings on the CPU kernel):
- About 75 CPU-h and under $15.
- It reuses everything, and the result is visible as surviving breeds in the atlas.

But it splits an already slow GA across worlds, so per-world progress drops. It addresses lineage collapse and generalisation rather than speed.

It pays once a substrate learns fast (the NCA or ES). Keep it for month 2. The LLM world writer is cheap but adds a review burden.

scores.name: C. Organ duplication and divergence: modules as units, grown along a task ladder (dot, mouse, text)
scores.why: It needs mouse and text worlds built first, and module sizes are hand-chosen. Visible progress on the current dot task is no better than a plain recurrent controller. It becomes relevant when the ladder arrives: duplicating a trained NCA lineage (an organ) is a cheap experiment then. The GALS multicore mapping (asynchronous between modules, synchronous inside) is hardware-friendly.

scores.name: D. Geometric genome with resolution growth: CPPN / ES-HyperNEAT with evolved local plasticity
scores.why: The zero-shot rescaling demo is cheap (about 2 GPU-days). But growth means re-querying a geometric function rather than development, the encoding is biased toward regular patterns, and the HyperNEAT rescaling claim is unverified. Expected visible progress on chase, growth or regrowth is lower than the NCA, whose shared local rule already transfers across size.

scores.name: C. Predictive tissue: every cell minimises its own prediction error (a predictive-coding graph, optionally spike-coded on the two channels)
scores.why: Week 1 yields a readout-prediction curve, not behaviour. Closed-loop control with predictive coding at 1-time-unit latency is unproven, and the 'dark room' problem (a tissue that avoids targets because they are surprising) is a real risk. The chance of nothing visible within a GPU-week is high. Revisit when the cursor and text worlds make prediction pay.

scores.name: Predictive tissue: every cell is a tiny local world model that learns during the life; evolution designs development and the learning rule (Baldwinian)
scores.why: A duplicate of the other predictive-tissue candidate, with the same issues: a local objective not aligned with F, collapse to trivial predictions, and little to gain in the reactive SPECK world. Its 1-2 week prototype is cheap, but its success criteria depend on a cursor-dynamics world that does not exist yet. Defer it to the cursor and text rungs.

judged.duplicates:
Clusters (build each once):
1. **Shared neural cell on a dense lattice (NCA family).** The four variants differ only in the trainer:
   - Grow-and-Act NCA: BPTT.
   - Vector-message tissue: BPTT, ES or both.
   - Shared in-context cell: ES.
   - Maturing tissue: ES plus plasticity.
2. **Logic tissue.** The DiffLogic-CA logic tissue (gradient first) and the bit-sliced gate-circuit tissue (CGP evolution first) share one runtime: one is the trainer, the other the referee.
3. **Meta-learned in-context learners.** The VSML learning tissue, the meta-learned cell-and-synapse programs (B), and the inner loop of the shared in-context cell.
4. **Three-factor plastic face synapses.** Plastic faces (A), the tensor spiking tissue's inner loop, the maturing tissue's synapse rule, and the object of the differentiable twin (D).
5. **Gradient twin or oracle on frozen bodies.** The differentiable twin (D), the tensor spiking tissue's oracle, and the EventProp item in cross-cutting.
6. **Predictive tissue.** Local-learning predictive tissue (C) and the Baldwinian local-world-model predictive tissue.
7. **Explicit growing graphs.** The developmental graph tissue (NDP/LNDP), Lamarckian morphing graphs (B), the axon slots and graph variants of the vector-message tissue and maturing tissue, and the module graph of organ duplication (C).
8. **Repeated cross-cutting items.** Each of these appears in nearly every angle, so treat them as shared infrastructure, not candidates:
   - Net2Net-style function-preserving growth, and gene duplication by halving outputs in the current kernel.
   - A clockless gate (train with update masks and delay jitter, then replay in the exact kernel).
   - ES with antithetic common-random-number pairs.
   - MAP-Elites, islands or speciation against lineage collapse.
   - Train small, deploy large.
judged.missing:
1. **Reuse the repo's own stepped torch tissue.**
   - src/develop.py (batched GRN development with diffusion and division claims), src/cells.py (quantised stepped LIF) and src/render.py (PIL GIFs) from the 2026-10-06 ladder are already a batched GPU-shaped simulator and viewer.
   - Every candidate plans a port from scratch. Starting from these files gives GIFs on day 1 and saves days of engineering.
   - Add one shared state-dump format that feeds the existing atlas template, so pilot bodies, NCA bodies and logic bodies can be watched side by side.

2. **No GPU is needed for the first watchable result.**
   - Measured [M]: 89 us per trained life-step (forward plus backward; 242 sites, 1.9k params, 64 lives, 32-step windows, 8 threads) on this laptop.
   - A Growing-NCA-scale run is about 30 min, so the whole debug loop (engine, world port, losses, async mask) can run locally at about $0.
   - Rent an L4 or 4090 only for scale and PBT.

3. **A visible-milestone ladder with kill rules.** Each milestone produces a GIF, has a time box, and stops a branch that fails:
   - M0: grow a shape on the hex prism and regrow it after a cut (hours; validates the engine).
   - M1: a fixed 7-19-cell tissue turns toward receptor pings.
   - M2: grow from 1 cell, then chase.
   - M3: delete half the body mid-life and watch it regrow and catch again.
   - M4: flip the sensor sign mid-life and watch it recover.

4. **The SHAC recipe for long horizons.** Short-horizon BPTT through a differentiable simulator plus a learned smooth critic for the tail. Xu et al. 2022, ICLR, https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.07137, opened; it reports more than 17x less training time on muscle-actuated locomotion. Candidates mention 'a critic' only in passing. This is the concrete fix for exploding gradients over 1,024-step lives and for the hard capture disk, and it uses the critic only during training.

5. **A behavioural-cloning warm start.**
   - Fit the NCA rule to the per-cell input/output of the hand-built reflex and of s5, taken from probe.py traces. That is minutes of training, and it yields a chasing body on day 1.
   - Then improve it with BPTT or ES on true F.
   - This doubles as the port-fidelity check.

6. **A cheap ceiling baseline.** PPO or ES on a fixed small RNN in the ported world, in hours. It calibrates the reachable F before anyone blames the substrate, and it is far cheaper than NEAT with morphisms or the spiking oracle.

7. **Hardware-faithful training from day 1, not at the end.**
   - Train with int8 fake quantisation, binary face messages through straight-through gradients, update mask p from 0.3 to 0.7, and delay jitter.
   - Log the asynchronous, quantised replay F on every checkpoint, so the sim-to-hardware gap is a tracked curve, not a final surprise.

8. **Free notebook GPUs** (Colab or Kaggle class) for the first L4-class runs. Availability and quotas are not verified.
judged.best_hybrid:
**What to build:** a hex-prism NCA cell that runs hardware-faithfully, trained by gradient plus ES, then compiled to logic. A CPU-only side track runs alongside.

**Weeks 0-1 (laptop, $0):**
- Port the CATCH/SPECK world as a stepped torch module, starting from src/develop.py and render.py.
- Hit M0: hex-prism growth and regrowth with an update mask of 0.5.
- Behavioural-clone the hand reflex into the shared per-site MLP:
  - 16 channels, 4-dimensional per-face messages, polarity-relative faces;
  - int8 fake quantisation and an optional binary message channel from the start.
- Check that the cloned rule reproduces the kernel's reflex F within noise.

**Week 2 (one rented L4 or 4090, about 1-2 days, under $50 [E]):**
- Pool training, so every life stays continuous: SHAC-style short-window BPTT on the expected-capture world plus a critic used only in training.
- PBT over 8 lineages, with R_cap rising from 1 to 2 to 3.
- Milestones M2 (grow from 1 cell, then chase) and M3 (half the body cut mid-life, then regrowth).

**Week 3:**
- An antithetic ES-with-common-random-numbers arm on the true Poisson F, fine-tuning the best lineages; this is the shared in-context cell's arm, and fitness is never shaped.
- Gates:
  - at least 90% of F kept under update mask p 0.3-0.7, delay jitter and int8;
  - F at least the re-tuned reflex at no more cells;
  - lateral_off costs at least 50% of F.

**Weeks 4-5:**
- Distil the winning rule's per-cell input/output into at most 2k DiffLogic gates, then harden.
- Run the result in the bit-sliced CPU engine (the bit-sliced logic tissue) with per-cell random update times as the exact asynchronous referee.
- Refine it there with CGP mutations.
- The netlist is the runtime that goes to the FPGA, so the sim-to-hardware gap ends at zero.

**CPU side track, in parallel on the existing kernel and viewers, no GPU:**
- ES with common random numbers against the GA at equal lives.
- The plastic-faces hand-set STDP test (s5 with chemical direction knocked out, under 1 CPU-h after about 1 week of kernel work).
- Gene duplication by halving outputs.

**Budget, roughly 3 engineering-weeks and under $100 [E]:**
- First growth GIF: 1-2 days.
- First grown chasing body: about 2 weeks.
- First regrowth-after-damage video: about 2.5 weeks.
- Hardware-native logic body: weeks 4-5.

**Later add-ons:**
- VSML fast weights for adaptation within a life.
- Axon slots in the gather representation.
- A parametric POET over worlds.

judged.judge:
Scientific risk and value. I asked five things of each candidate: how strong the evidence is and at what scale; how it would likely fail; what would be new if it worked; how decisive a cheap first prototype would be; and whether a result would still teach us about emergent local computation. Under the binding clarifications I also weighed how native and cheap the organism's runtime would be on silicon, the gap between the training simulator and that runtime, and how fast a visible outcome appears.

Grounding:
- I read RESULTS.md (2026-10-09 pilot section) and docs/POST_PILOT_CALLS.md, and checked src/life/handbuilt.py.
  - The GRN-grown router genome (GS5) exists. It scores +8.90 over a whole life, level with the reflex.
  - The hand router leads the reflex by +2.2 F only in base SPECK. Its lead is about 0 with a twin target, near placement or decoy-lite, and -1.28 with sparse receptors.
- I inspected the bit-slice benchmark in scratchpad/alt/hardware/bitslice3.c: one ring neighbour instead of 8 faces, no world, no growth.
- Web search was exhausted for this session. New citations were checked by opening arXiv abstract pages or running arXiv API queries.
  - OpenArchEvo (arXiv 2609.40258) exists, dated 2026-09-30.
  - An arXiv API query for papers that mention "neural cellular automata" plus control, agent or locomotion, newest first (15 entries, back to 2023), found no NCA that grows a body and steers it within one life. That supports the GA-NCA novelty claim, but the query was narrow, so it is not a full literature check.

scores.name: Grow-and-Act NCA (GA-NCA): one shared neural rule per lattice site, trained by gradient through whole lives
scores.why: Strongest evidence base of the new substrates for growth and regeneration under asynchronous masks: Growing NCA pool training, IsoNCA polarity, Sensorimotor Lenia and the NCA cart-pole. Per-voxel spiking NCAs already steer soft robots using only local information (Nadizar et al. 2022, arXiv 2204.02099, not cited by the pass). A win would be new (my arXiv query found no grow-and-steer NCA) and very visible: growth plus chasing you can watch. The prototype is decisive because it starts with a port check (the hand reflex run as a fixed rule must reproduce the kernel's F). Risks: (1) 1,024-step BPTT through a soft-capture proxy pushes toward the shaped-score failure the repo has already seen. (2) Lockstep exploits. (3) As the organism runtime it is the weakest of the top three: about 4.7k float MACs per site per step, and the gap from float training to int8 asynchronous replay is unmeasured. (4) Measured 222 ms per life on CPU, so it needs rented GPUs. Best value is as a fast teacher that gets compiled into the logic tissue.

scores.name: Developmental graph tissue: cells that grow their own directed wires, with function-preserving division (NDP/LNDP-style)
scores.why: Thin evidence at the needed scale: the NDP solves CartPole with about 10 nodes but not LunarLander (116 against 200), and LNDP works at about 100 nodes. Edge growth needs degree caps and costs, which are new hard-coded rules. ES in about 5k dimensions on Poisson F carries the same noise problem as the GA. Attention-based wiring by gather/scatter is the least cheap runtime here. A negative result could not separate 'graph tissue is bad' from 'ES was too noisy'. Keep its two transferable parts as features elsewhere: Net2Net division with a bitwise no-change unit test, and radius-bounded axons paid per unit length.

scores.name: Logic tissue: differentiable-logic CA cells with binary spike messages, compiled to exact gates
scores.why: The same paradigm as the hardware pass's logic tissue, so merge them. This version leads with the riskier half, gradient training first: DiffLogic CA needed heavy tuning even for static patterns, no DiffLogic agent or control result is published, and relaxed BPTT through a world over long horizons is unproven. Its useful contribution is the distillation route (a teacher rule compiled to 2k gates or fewer) and evaluating only the hardened rule. Keep both in the merged candidate. Measured 21.6 ms per life in a numpy stand-in.

scores.name: Learning tissue: two-stream cells that meta-learn a local learning rule (VSML/BLUR inside the NCA)
scores.why: VSML and BLUR evidence is small-scale and mostly supervised. Meta-training over whole lives is unstable and costly. It only pays in worlds that vary per life, and those do not exist yet. Fast-weight state on every face enlarges the hardware tile, and the result is hard to interpret. Revisit as an add-on only after a base substrate shows that within-life adaptation pays.

scores.name: A. Plastic faces: evolved three-factor STDP on per-face synapses, inherited at division (keeps the clockless kernel)
scores.why: Best scientific value per CPU-hour, with zero sim-to-hardware gap: the exact clockless kernel stays the runtime, and trace STDP times an eligibility-modulator factor is what Loihi- and ReckOn-class silicon already implements. The first test is a falsifiable, project-specific prediction. Knock out chemical direction (s5 loses 10.1 F); pair STDP driven by the measured sense-to-act timing of about 1.0 time unit should then rebuild 'excite from below, inhibit from above'. It costs under 1 CPU-h on 256 paired lives, and the learned weight map can be plotted. It attacks a measured bottleneck (direction comes only from costly chemistry that breaks at a slower gene clock) and the 'learn small, inherit at division' goal. Risks: runaway excitation (needs homeostasis); evolution may set learning rates to zero in a stationary world; a negative at only 3-5 hand-set settings says little, so sweep more widely. Novelty is moderate.

scores.name: B. Meta-learned cell and synapse programs (a VSML-style tissue) trained on GPUs
scores.why: Duplicates the VSML learning tissue and the shared in-context cell, with the highest meta-training cost (the VeLO caution) and the least interpretability. ES over 1,000-step unrolls of a black-box tissue scored on Poisson F combines the two hardest risks in this whole set. The fidelity gate (the reflex within 5% in JAX) is good and is reused elsewhere.

scores.name: C. Predictive tissue: every cell minimises its own prediction error (a predictive-coding graph, optionally spike-coded on the two channels)
scores.why: It would give the hidden planes a job and fits the later cursor and text worlds. But the evidence is supervised and static; closed-loop control within about 1 time unit, while relaxing to equilibrium, is unproven. Dark-room and 'good predictor, poor actor' failures are likely, and the local objective is a hard-coded rule. The week-1 test (the hidden plane predicts the target ahead better than persistence) is cheap but does not test the task. Duplicate of the Baldwinian predictive tissue; keep for later.

scores.name: D. Differentiable twin for meta-plasticity: a gradient outer loop for rule parameters, evolution for development, the exact kernel as referee
scores.why: The twin's F against the kernel's F over dt is a missing measurement, and it directly quantifies the gap between the training simulator and the runtime. Keeping the exact kernel as the only judge is the right design. But the 'search or substrate' question is already partly answered: the hand GRN router (GS5) grows in the same kernel and scores +8.90 over a life, and the planned D2 (router-seeded arm) and D3 (4x lives) test search against noise more cheaply. Surrogate-gradient BPTT over 1,000+ spiking steps on an expected-capture loss risks the parking failure. Merge with the oracle of the tensor spiking tissue; EventProp on the kernel could replace the twin for face weights.

scores.name: A. Maturing tissue: GPU neural-CA cells with neutral division and evolved plasticity
scores.why: Good ingredients: silent newborns whose maturation the GRN controls, a 'birth deficit' readout, per-edge three-factor weights, and 64-256 CRN lives per genome. But it changes substrate, learning rule, growth law and optimiser at once, so neither a success nor a failure could be attributed. The pieces are better tested separately: plastic faces in the kernel, GA-NCA on a GPU, neutral duplication in the GRN.

scores.name: B. Lamarckian morphing graphs: NEAT with function-preserving morphisms and a gradient/e-prop inner loop, tensorized on GPU
scores.why: It drops development and within-life growth, so the hardware runtime would no longer grow. It trains on a clock with a proxy loss, and morphisms are only approximately function-preserving for LIF thresholds. Its stated purpose, a 'best-case ML reference', is served more cheaply and more clearly by a centralised policy trained on the same sensors, which gives the task ceiling directly.

scores.name: C. Organ duplication and divergence: modules as units, grown along a task ladder (dot, mouse, text)
scores.why: Module size and port counts are chosen by hand. Evidence in this setting is weak: the ML evidence is MoE and LLM-scale, the biology comparative. It needs a task ladder (mouse, text) that is not built, so nothing visible within days. Keep 'duplicate a progenitor lineage' as a later mutation operator.

scores.name: D. Geometric genome with resolution growth: CPPN / ES-HyperNEAT with evolved local plasticity
scores.why: Biased toward regular patterns, and a geometric genome is less emergent. Its key supporting claim (a HyperNEAT network evolved at low resolution works at higher resolution) was not verified by the pass. The zero-shot 4x rescale test is cheap and crisp, but shared local rules (NCA, logic) already give size-independence with more locality.

scores.name: Logic tissue: evolved and differentiable gate-circuit cells that exchange spike bits, simulated bit-sliced
scores.why: The only paradigm whose evolved artefact is the runtime itself: netlist to LUTs or standard cells. If the hardware runs synchronous steps with per-cell LFSR update masks, the sim-to-hardware gap is zero by construction, and asynchronous replay stays as a robustness test. The measured stand-in gave 2.6-7.6 ms per life per core. Checked: one ring neighbour rather than 8 faces, no world or growth, and the compiled variant needs a per-genome compile, so expect about 10-15x in practice. Bit-slicing forces 64-256 CRN lives per genome, which is what a per-life reliability of 0.026 needs. Novel: no published logic-CA agent, closed-loop or evolved. Risks: CGP on large, noisy, closed-loop growing tissue may stall, and integrators cost gates. Start with positive controls (distil reflex@hollow3 and the GS5 router from probe traces) to separate expressivity from search. Laptop only, days.

scores.name: Tensor spiking tissue on a GPU: ES at large population with antithetic common lives, evolved three-factor plasticity, and a gradient oracle
scores.why: This bundles three experiments. Two are cheap and decisive: antithetic ES with CRN against the GA on the existing CPU kernel (no port needed), and the dt-equivalence curve. The full GPU port costs 6-14 person-weeks for a 2-9x gain by the repo's own estimate, which is poor value. The oracle overlaps the GS5 router evidence and the planned D2/D3, and the plasticity part duplicates plastic faces. Split it: keep ES with CRN and the dt curve, drop the port.

scores.name: Vector-message tissue (NCA-style): a shared recurrent cell rule trained by gradients through development and behaviour, inside an evolutionary or PBT outer loop, grown by curriculum
scores.why: Duplicate of GA-NCA. It adds a better representation (a list of occupied cells with a neighbour table, plus axon slots) and a three-arm comparison (BPTT, ES, warm start then ES) that improves what can be attributed. But it measured 0.31-0.67 s per life on CPU and rates itself the weakest hardware fit. Fold its representation and arms into GA-NCA.

scores.name: CellCode: LLM-guided evolution of the cell's event handlers (AlphaEvolve-style), checked by the exact clockless kernel
scores.why: Novel: no LLM evolution of a developmental, event-driven tissue was found. It keeps every substrate preference. Zero sim-to-hardware gap: integer handlers with bounded loops compile into the integer ABI. Cheap: about 15 CPU-h plus a modest LLM spend. Designed as science: a 16/64/256-life cascade with CRN, an AutoML-Zero random-mutation control arm and a kill criterion. Sharp risks: FunSearch and AlphaEvolve successes had cheap, low-noise evaluators, while per-life reliability here is 0.026. The LLM prior injects designed roles, so a win may teach more about LLM priors than about emergent local computation unless the observable whitelist and control arm hold. API model drift hurts reproducibility. A dark horse with high novelty.

scores.name: Shared in-context cell on GPU: one meta-learned recurrent rule in every cell, vector messages, evolution strategies over a varied world distribution
scores.why: Duplicate of GA-NCA, with ES instead of BPTT. Drawing the world from a distribution every life, so that only within-life adaptation scores well, is a valuable idea worth reusing. But ES in about 10k dimensions on Poisson F is the selection-noise problem at larger scale. The transfer from synchronous training to asynchronous running is untested, and the project's v1 already collapsed under asynchrony. Use its world-distribution idea inside GA-NCA.

scores.name: Open-ended world-body co-evolution with foundation-model curators (POET, OMNI-EPIC and ASAL around the existing substrate)
scores.why: It targets two measured problems. Runs collapse to one lineage by generation 2-119. The routing niche is narrow in world space: the router's lead is +2.2 in base SPECK, about 0 in the twin, near and decoy-lite worlds, and -1.28 with sparse receptors. The parametric v0 runs on CPU only and cheaply. But open-ended loops are hard to judge, splitting compute across worlds deepens the noise problem, and LLM-written worlds risk leaks. Its strongest near-term value is a pre-registered held-out world panel used as evaluation infrastructure for every paradigm, not as the first build.

scores.name: Predictive tissue: every cell is a tiny local world model that learns during the life; evolution designs development and the learning rule (Baldwinian)
scores.why: Better designed than the other predictive candidate. It has learning on/off and inheritance on/off arms, a mid-life switch, and the Baldwin signal measured as a smaller drop from parent to child. The event-driven version keeps the runtime exact. But local predictive learning driving closed-loop action is not demonstrated. Collapse to trivial predictions is likely without contrastive targets, and it needs the cursor-prediction world built first. Keep it for when prediction tasks arrive.
